evals.prompt: An agent was asked to fix one flaky test. Twenty tool calls later, it has refactored the entire test harness, added a new mocking library, and hasn't touched the actual flaky test yet. What happened and what should have caught it earlier?
evals.expected_output: Names this as goal drift specifically (not generic 'confusion') and recommends periodic re-anchoring against the original one-sentence objective, rather than a vague 'be more careful' fix.

assertions.text: Names the specific drift mechanism (goal drift)
Recommends re-anchoring against the original objective

evals.prompt: Our long-running agent keeps losing track of earlier constraints as the conversation grows. Someone suggested just switching to a model with a much bigger context window to fix it. Will that work?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a bigger context window delays when drift becomes visible but does not fix the underlying mechanisms (context drift, role drift, etc.) - recommends active mitigations like re-injecting key constraints or compression instead.

assertions.text: States a bigger window does not fix the underlying problem
Recommends an active mitigation instead of just more context
